(accord. to Uṇ. i, 33 fr. √ 2. श्लिष्) a servant, slave, dependant, L.
a profligate or low person, L.
n. astronomy, astrology, L.
n. exhaustion, L.
1. श्लिष् (cf. √ 1. श्रिष्) cl. 1. P. श्लेषति, to burn, Dhātup. xvii, 52.
clinging, embracing, L.
clinging or adhering to (loc. or comp.), Kāṭh.; KātyŚr.; MBh. &c.
(with सर्वतः) adhering closely, fitting tight (as a coat of mail), MBh. vii, 5161
adhering to one's self i.e. not affecting others, merely personal (as an art or science), Mālav. i, 15 (v.l. शिष्ट)
joined together, united, connected, MBh.; Kāv. &c.
clasped, embraced, Kāv.; Kathās.
(in rhet.) connected so as to be susceptible of a double interpretation, equivocal, Sāh.
श्लिष्ट—परम्परित-रूपक n. a continuous series of words having a double meaning (a kind of metaphor), Śiś., Sch.
श्लिष्ट—रूपक n. ambiguity as a metaphor, Kāv. ii, 87.
श्लिष्ट—वर्त्मन् n. the adhering together of the eyelids, ŚārṅgS.
an objection expressed through using words containing a double meaning, Kāvyād. ii, 159; 160.
a Dīpaka (q.v.) containing a double meaning, ib. ii, 113; 114.
an expression containing a d˚ m˚, Kathās.
adherence, connection, MW.
an embrace, ib.
N. of a son of Dhruva, Hariv.; VP.
(thought by some to be fr. √ श्लिष् + पद; others suppose श्ली to have the meaning ‘elephant’) morbid enlargement of the leg, swelled leg, elephantiasis, Suśr.; Bhpr. &c.
श्ली-पद—प्रभव m. ‘source of elephantiasis’, the Mango tree, L.
‘removing or curing elephantiasis’, the tree Putranjiva Roxburghii, L.
having a swelled leg, suffering from elephantiasis
a club-footed man, Mn. iii, 165
(= श्रीर; cf. अ-श्लील) prosperous, fortunate, affluent, happy, W.
